title: Move interactivity into a small Client Component
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/counter.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
import { useState } from 'react';
export default function Counter(){ const [n,setN]=useState(0); return <button onClick={()=>setN(n+1)}>{n}</button>; }

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Build a Server Component page importing Counter.
Click repeatedly and verify the count.
Inspect the client graph and confirm the data-access module was not imported.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: State and event handlers require a client boundary.
Build a Server Component page importing Counter.
alternativeApproaches: Do not import a server-only data component into the client graph. Compose it in a Server Component parent and pass its rendered output through a slot such as children; that preserves ownership of the server work.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
